subject: ACME request: shorten notice window & clarify termination-for-convenience
messages:
From: Leah Barnes <leah.barnes@acme.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.io
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 12:42:00 -0400
Subject: Termination flexibility & notice window - redline request

Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — team is excited about the performance gains. Legal and procurement reviewed the MSA and attached a redline (ACME_Redlines_v1.docx). Two items they asked us to surface and negotiate before we can move to signature:

1) Notice window for non-renewal: they want a 30-day notice instead of 60 days.
2) Termination for convenience: they asked for a reciprocal 60-day termination for convenience right with a pro-rated refund for unused prepaid committed capacity.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on both? If Redwood is open to shortening the non-renewal notice and adding a reciprocal termination for convenience (with standard smoothing), procurement would be willing to proceed to legal sign-off this week.

I've attached our redline. Happy to hop on a 30m call to align.

Best,
Leah Barnes
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp
Attachment: ACME_Redlines_v1.docx (docx)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Leah Barnes <leah.barnes@acme.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Termination flexibility & notice window - redline request

Leah —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Appreciate the fast turnaround. I looped in Ben (Contracts) and Laura (Legal ops) so we can respond with proposed language and an internal fallback. High-level position:

- Notice window: we can consider 30 days for pilot / PoC customers, but for committed reserved capacity we generally require 60 days to plan capacity and avoid stranded GPUs. Would you confirm whether Acme plans to use reserved capacity or hosted on-demand?
- Termination for convenience: Redwood typically offers a negotiated TFC only for enterprise customers with a defined offboarding plan and potential wind-down fees. We can propose a reciprocal 60-day TFC with a defined refund schedule (prorated by full months remaining, minus provisioning costs).

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to prepare a tracked redline of the MSA focusing on Sections 2 (Term), 3 (Renewal), and 7 (Termination).
- Quick 20m sync tomorrow to align on the refund schedule and whether Acme needs reserved capacity commitments.

Available times: Tue 11:00am PT or Tue 3:00pm PT. Let me know which works and I’ll send a calendar invite + Ben's draft redline.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Leah Barnes <leah.barnes@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 09:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Termination flexibility & notice window - proposed redlines (internal note)

Internal note (forwarding for visibility). Key negotiation points and proposed fallback language:

1) 30 vs 60 day notice for non-renewal
- Proposed capture: for all Order Forms with Reserved Capacity, 60-day notice; for Order Forms flagged as "Pilot" or "Evaluation" in Exhibit A, 30-day notice. Simple boolean in Order Form prevents legal churn.

2) Termination for convenience (TFC) reciprocity and refunds
- Proposed capture: Reciprocal 60-day TFC available for Enterprise Order Forms with at least 6 months initial term. Refund = (prepaid fees for full unused months) - (one-time provisioning & decommissioning charge equal to 10% of remaining prepaid fees, capped at $25k). Add an offboarding plan requirement in Schedule 2.

3) Operational fallback for capacity
- If customer opts for 30-day non-renewal but has Reserved Capacity, include a 30-day notice with a one-time transition fee equal to two weeks of committed capacity invoice.

I will attach the tracked changes in Redwood_MSA_Redline_v2.docx and share with Leah after Vanessa confirms we’re aligned. Laura — any objections to the decommissioning charge or the wording around Exhibit A pilot flag?

-Ben
Contracts Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_MSA_Redline_v2.docx (docx)

From: Leah Barnes <leah.barnes@acme.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Termination flexibility & notice window - redline request

Vanessa / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. Acme confirms the initial Order Form will be Reserved Capacity (12-month term) but we can label the first 60 days as a "ramp" period. Procurement is comfortable with the Exhibit A pilot flag approach as long as the Order Form explicitly marks pilot status for the first 90 days. The proposed refund calculation looks reasonable, but Legal asked to cap the decommissioning charge at $15k (they want lower up-front friction).

We are OK to proceed if Redwood: 
- Accepts the Exhibit A pilot flag (30-day notice during pilot)
- Lowers the decommissioning charge cap to $15k

If you can incorporate those two changes into the tracked redline and send the DocuSign packet, procurement will sign and we can start onboarding next week.

Leah Barnes
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp
Attachment: None
